name: Marxism–Leninism
summary: Marxism-Leninism is the communist ideology built on Marx and Lenin and codified under Stalin, the official doctrine of the Soviet Union and of states such as China, Vietnam and Cuba. It holds that capitalism must be overthrown by revolution led by a disciplined vanguard party, which then rules a one-party socialist state as the dictatorship of the proletariat. That state owns the main means of production, plans the economy and works toward a classless, stateless communist society. Its philosophy is dialectical and historical materialism, including class struggle as the engine of history and atheism.
scope: The classical doctrine as set out by Lenin (What Is To Be Done?, The State and Revolution, The Right of Nations to Self-Determination) and codified by Stalin (Dialectical and Historical Materialism), with the 1977 Soviet Constitution as the program of a mature Marxist-Leninist state. Where post-Mao China and Vietnam diverge (market reforms) the answer is marked as split. Trotskyism, Maoism, Hoxhaism and Western Marxism are excluded.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free medical care from state health institutions is a constitutional guarantee of the Marxist-Leninist state model.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Communist parties back workers' immediate economic demands, but Lenin treats wage struggles as trade-union politics that cannot by themselves end exploitation, so support is real but secondary.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine holds that socialist ownership and state plans avoid the crises of capitalist markets and should replace them.

public-ownership.rationale: State ownership of land, minerals and major industry is the economic foundation of the socialist state.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Adherents want the wealth of the capitalist class taken over entirely; heavier taxes are welcomed as a step but seen as reformist rather than the goal.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are given a role in managing socialist society, but Lenin held that unions left to themselves produce only trade-union consciousness and need party leadership.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production is abolished; only personal property from earned income is protected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents go further than regulation and want large firms nationalized, so they favor tighter control in the meantime.

cut-welfare.rationale: Pensions, social insurance, cheap housing and free education are constitutional rights in the Marxist-Leninist state.

worker-ownership.rationale: Marxism-Leninism favors ownership by the state on behalf of the whole people over ownership by each enterprise's own workers, though collective farms are accepted as a transitional form.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The socialist state is expected to suppress counter-revolution and its security services did so extensively, so security monitoring is accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the principle that personal freedoms must not harm the interests of society and the state.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Advocating racial or national exclusiveness or hostility is made punishable by law.

strong-leader.rationale: The doctrine rejects parliamentary deadlock in favor of decisive party leadership; it officially prefers collective leadership to one person, though Stalin's rule shows the practice.

state-harmful.rationale: The state will eventually wither away under full communism, but for the whole transition a strong proletarian state is held to be necessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Lenin wrote of an armed working population, while Marxist-Leninist states kept arms in state hands; the theory gives no settled answer on private ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: In capitalist states the police and army are seen as instruments of class rule, while in a socialist state defense is a sacred duty; answered here as adherents living under capitalism would.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the view that commodifying labor and persons is capitalist exploitation; Marxist-Leninist states treated prostitution as a social ill to abolish rather than legalize.

decide-locally.rationale: Democratic centralism binds lower bodies to the decisions of higher ones, and Lenin argued for a centralized organization.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the materialist view that behavior is shaped by social conditions; Marxist-Leninist states described their penal labor as re-education.

traditional-family.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states placed the family under state protection, though Marxist theory criticizes the bourgeois family; mainstream practice was pro-family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states persecuted homosexuality for most of their history; some modern parties have changed, so this reflects the historical mainstream.

abortion-legal.rationale: Soviet policy shifted between legalization and bans; the long-run Soviet norm after 1955 was legal abortion, inferred alongside the commitment to women's equality.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states practiced state atheism, separated church from state and protected atheistic propaganda.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-imperialism and the ban on national or racial hostility make combating racial oppression a stated aim.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from historical materialism, which explains social roles as products of material conditions rather than fixed nature.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states promoted patriotism and national cultures 'national in form, socialist in content', while subordinating them to proletarian internationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Stalin's text states that capitalism cannot be reformed away gradually and that one must be a revolutionary, not a reformist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which rejects dividing workers by nation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on state sovereignty and non-intervention and suspicion of bodies dominated by imperialist powers.

free-trade.rationale: Lenin's theory of imperialism treats capitalist trade and capital export as the mechanism of colonial exploitation.

nation-first.rationale: Proletarian internationalism and solidarity with socialist countries and national liberation struggles take priority, though socialism in one country gave weight to the Soviet state's interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents reject Western humanitarian intervention as imperialism and uphold non-intervention, while backing national liberation struggles.

open-borders.rationale: The final goal is a stateless, classless world society, which implies no borders, though Marxist-Leninist states closed theirs.

limit-growth.rationale: Developing the productive forces is central, and Marxist-Leninist states pursued rapid industrialization.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the state's duty to protect nature and the preference for planned rather than market responses.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Productive forces drive history, but technology alone is not enough without changing ownership relations.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to developing productive forces and the Soviet pursuit of nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution is held to be natural and necessary to replace capitalism; Stalin quotes Marx that force is the midwife of every old society.

experts-over-public.rationale: Lenin held that socialist consciousness has to be brought to workers from outside by a theoretically trained vanguard rather than arising spontaneously.

central-planning.rationale: State five-year plans directing the economy define the Marxist-Leninist economic model.

socialized-markets.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy rejected markets after the New Economic Policy, while today's Chinese and Vietnamese Marxist-Leninists accept a socialist market economy; adherents are split.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: land is to be nationalized outright, so a tax on privately held land is a reformist half-measure.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the rule that property may not be a source of unearned income.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution under socialism is by work, with a right and duty to work, not by unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the socialist state's control of the economy and of foreign trade under the plan.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state plans the development of the whole economy and directs investment through it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Small peasant property was collectivized and the kulaks dispossessed; socialist ownership replaces small property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: In the higher phase of communism, distribution follows 'to each according to his needs', ending pay by labor.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of the means of production and planned control of the economy, which a state bank serves.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Adherents reject attempts to harmonize the interests of capitalists and workers, though unions and work collectives take part in managing a socialist economy.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Communist Party is the leading and guiding force of society and the core of the political system.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Monarchy is seen as a feudal form of class rule that revolution overthrows.

democracy-best.rationale: Lenin called capitalist democracy democracy for a minority and dissolved the Constituent Assembly after losing its election.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums are allowed but major direction is set by the vanguard party rather than popular votes.

workers-councils.rationale: Power is held to belong to the people through the Soviets, which Lenin set against bourgeois parliaments, though under party leadership.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin defined national self-determination as the right to secede, and the Soviet constitution kept it formally, though it was rarely allowed in practice.

natural-rulers.rationale: Historical materialism explains rule by class position rather than innate fitness, though the vanguard is seen as the most conscious section of the class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolutionary force is held to be necessary for social transformation.

war-builds-character.rationale: Lenin denounced patriotic war between capitalist powers; wars are judged by their class character, not as good for a nation.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1977 constitution separates the church from the state and protects atheistic propaganda.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Dialectical materialism rejects religion as a basis for anything, and Marxist-Leninist states were atheist.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defense and law enforcement are functions of the socialist state, and private enterprise of this kind is ruled out.

military-superiority.rationale: Defense of the socialist motherland is a sacred duty and the USSR sought military strength against imperialism, alongside official peaceful coexistence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The USSR was defined as a multinational state and advocating national exclusiveness was punishable.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Historical materialism holds that class struggle between exploiters and exploited drives history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Full communism aims at distribution by need, but the socialist phase accepts unequal pay according to work.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from support for national self-determination and autonomy, limited by state ownership of land.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and support for national liberation struggles.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unity is to be based on class and socialism, not shared religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Marxist-Leninist ethics promotes collectivism and rejects income from exploitation and private gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights are inseparable from duties and may not be exercised against the interests of society and the state.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from a materialism that treats nature as knowable matter to be mastered, though the state also protects nature.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from Marxist rejection of the idea that population, rather than capitalism, causes poverty; China's later policy is an exception.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrialization and growth of the productive forces are the material basis of socialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Productive forces are the most revolutionary element of society, and adherents favor rapid technical development under socialist ownership.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from enthusiasm for science and the aim of a new socialist person, not stated directly.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Lenin saw administration as simple accounting, but the doctrine keeps political direction with the party; there is no settled view.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the rule that individual freedoms must not harm the interests of the socialist state.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine looks forward to new modes of production and treats restoring older orders as reaction.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy is to follow the scientific laws of Marxist theory, though later reformers like Deng Xiaoping stressed practical results.

direct-action.rationale: Change is to come through revolution led by the vanguard party, though Leninists also take part in elections and parliaments as a platform rather than as the path to socialism.

means-match-ends.rationale: A dictatorship and a strong coercive state are held to be the necessary road to a classless, stateless society, so the means are expressly unlike the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Historical materialism treats the growth of the productive forces as progress and the material basis of socialism, the opposite of returning to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Lenin quotes Marx that the higher phase of communism ends the enslaving subordination of the individual to the division of labor, though under socialism specialized work and pay by work remain.

distribute-by-need.rationale: 'From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs' is the stated principle of the higher phase of communism.

production-for-use.rationale: The socialist state declares that the aim of social production is to meet people's growing material and cultural needs, and private ownership for profit is abolished.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The doctrine holds that the capitalist owner lives by exploiting wage labor, and the socialist constitution forbids property being used to obtain unearned income.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The dictatorship of the proletariat to suppress the exploiters during the transition to communism is the core of Lenin's State and Revolution.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization of agriculture was a defining policy of Marxist-Leninist states, with collective-farm property written into the constitution.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin's theory of imperialism as the highest stage of capitalism, driving the powers to war over markets and colonies, is a core tenet of the doctrine.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is entitled to take and redistribute the social product; adherents object to unearned income from property, not to the state's claim on earnings.

harm-principle.rationale: Citizens' freedoms may not be exercised to the detriment of society and the state, a far wider limit than harm to other individuals.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nations hold a right to self-determination up to secession, and the constitution gives union republics collective rights.

conscription.rationale: The constitution makes defense of the socialist motherland a sacred duty and military service an honorable obligation of citizens.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist states restricted emigration and located popular power in the soviets under the party, and the idea of disciplining a state by leaving it belongs to market thinking the doctrine rejects.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is understood as an instrument of class rule that should serve the working people, and treating citizens as customers belongs to the commodity relations socialism abolishes.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's view that real power in a bourgeois democracy lies with the capitalist class, which the press and elected officials alike serve.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Historical materialism explains differences between peoples by social and material conditions, and the socialist state banned propaganda of racial or national exclusiveness.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through soviets of deputies and the party, not through families or trade bodies; the corporatist idea of harmonizing classes is rejected, though work collectives have a role.

total-state.rationale: The party leads and the state plans the economy, education and culture in the communist spirit, though the doctrine expects the state to wither away and protects personal property and the family.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine frames change as class revolution toward a new mode of production, not as the rebirth of a decayed nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Official doctrine condemns imperialism and annexations and commits the socialist state to peaceful coexistence and the territorial integrity of states, though Soviet practice diverged.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal relations of personal dependence are a stage of class exploitation that history and revolution leave behind.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is described as feudal exploitation of the serf by the lord, abolished by the advance to later modes of production.

universal-morality.rationale: Historical materialism treats ideas, morality included, as reflections of the material conditions and class relations of each epoch rather than timeless truths.

single-common-good.rationale: The party claims a scientific theory of society that sets one correct line and rejects pluralist bargaining, though in class society it sees no common good between classes.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Lenin rejected Zionism as reactionary bourgeois nationalism and, after brief support for partition in 1947-48, the Soviet line condemned Zionism as an ideology of the Jewish bourgeoisie allied to imperialism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism and the rejection of ethnically defined nationhood, which make citizenship by ancestry foreign to the doctrine.

revive-national-language.rationale: Lenin held that there must be no compulsory official language, while Marxist-Leninist states promoted the languages peoples actually spoke.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The 1977 Constitution has work collectives take part in deciding production and public affairs and Soviets as the form of power, though always under party leadership rather than as an independent vote over management.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is a free state-run system guaranteed by the constitution, so funding private school choice contradicts the doctrine; vouchers themselves are not mentioned.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from state ownership and the central plan, which direct investment without a revenue constraint, so adherents do not treat borrowing for demand as the issue; Soviet budgets were nonetheless meant to balance.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marxist-Leninists hold that political freedom under capitalism is bourgeois freedom, and the socialist state abolishes private ownership of the main means of production and plans the economy under the party's leadership.

rule-by-example.rationale: Lenin treats the state and law as instruments of class rule to be used firmly in the dictatorship of the proletariat, and the 1977 Constitution rests order on party leadership, socialist legality and citizens' duties; rule by moral example is not the doctrine's mechanism, an inference at low confidence.

national-self-determination.rationale: Lenin defends the right of nations to self-determination, meaning the right to secede and form independent states, as a core part of the national programme.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed directly: inferred from Leninist treatment of war as a class question rather than a legal one, and from Soviet practice of intervening in allied states without Security Council approval, though the 1977 Constitution also professes respect for sovereignty and peaceful coexistence.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dialectical and historical materialism claims to be a scientific worldview, and the state promoted atheism and treated religion as ideology to be overcome, so reason and science are the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Proletarian internationalism puts class above nationality, and the 1977 Constitution guarantees foreigners in the USSR the rights provided by law, but its social rights are framed for citizens, so this is inferred rather than stated.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats formal freedoms as hollow without material security, and the constitution guarantees work, housing, education and health as real rights.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Lenin's socialist principle is that he who does not work shall not eat, and the constitution makes socially useful work a duty and honour of every able-bodied citizen.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin held that class antagonism is irreconcilable and that the workers' party must lead the struggle against employers, not conciliate them.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The constitution makes preserving historical monuments and cultural values a civic duty, and the doctrine claims to inherit past culture while remaking it.

dominated-front.rationale: Lenin called for alliance of the proletariat with oppressed nations against imperialism, though the doctrine frames it as class and anti-imperialist rather than a Western-versus-rest front.

workers-nation.rationale: Proletarian internationalism is a core principle: workers of all nations share interests, and the constitution makes internationalist duty a citizen obligation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The constitution declares that women and men have equal rights in all fields.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed as a legal ban; inferred from state control of credit and banking and a Soviet system that paid interest on savings, with no doctrinal prohibition of interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The constitution guarantees equal rights to citizens of different races and nationalities, and the doctrine opposes national oppression.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Lenin, following Marx, defines the state as an organ of class rule, which the proletariat must seize and eventually let wither away.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the doctrine's push to build up the productive forces, which in Soviet practice meant heavy coal, oil and gas output.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Lenin opposes compulsory assimilation and a compulsory state language, defending each nation's culture and language as long as it is socialist in content.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from class analysis: migration is driven by capital's demand for cheap labor, not by a deliberate plot against a native population.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed directly; Lenin scorns bourgeois parliamentarism and the Soviet system elected deputies by district under the Party's leading role, so party-proportional seats were not a goal.

national-mission.rationale: Proletarian internationalism and support for world revolution mean the ideology wants socialist government to spread, though through class struggle rather than national mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: Engels-derived theory ties women's subordination to class society, but the Soviet constitution holds that equality has been achieved, so adherents see the problem as rooted in capitalism and largely solved.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lenin describes bourgeois democracy and its politicians as instruments of capital, serving the ruling class rather than ordinary people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine stresses social conditions over heredity, and the Soviet state rejected eugenics policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: the state's organs are seen as instruments of class rule answerable to the Party, and the constitution provides no mechanism for prosecuting past state violence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is to own the main means of production, plan the economy and direct social life, which is the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Proletarian internationalism and the constitutional ban on national and racial hostility make discouraging marriage across racial lines contrary to doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality of citizens before the law regardless of origin, though class enemies were historically denied rights, so equal worth is not unqualified.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialism in one country, set out by Stalin and codified as doctrine, holds that socialism can be built in a single state without waiting for world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist line and the Soviet view of Zionism as bourgeois nationalism; adherents applied this to Israel but the general claim was not codified.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states replaced religious family law with a single secular state family law for all citizens.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: the state protects atheist propaganda while limiting religious propaganda to worship (Soviet practice), but doctrine itself centers on freedom of conscience.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from state atheism and a materialist view that sacred-animal protection is superstition; the doctrine never addressed cattle slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The 1977 constitution separates the school from the church, so state schools give no religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin held that the state must be strengthened while capitalist encirclement persists, and the withering away was postponed to full communism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy rests on the proletariat's historical role led by the vanguard party, not on consent through elections, which Lenin called bourgeois democracy.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Historical materialism treats ruling ideas as those of the ruling class and theory as partisan, though Marxism-Leninism also claims its own science is objectively true.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred: foreign trade was a state monopoly serving the plan, and Lenin's imperialism theory treats the drive for export markets as a capitalist pathology, so a surplus was not a goal in itself.

population-transfer.rationale: The doctrine and constitution forbid national hostility and uphold self-determination, though Stalin's regime deported whole peoples in practice.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolution by force and the dictatorship of the proletariat are central, and the doctrine rejects pacifist and reformist renunciation of violence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The engine of history is class struggle, not competition between individuals or peoples, and the doctrine stresses international solidarity and planned cooperation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states wrote the leading role of the Party into the constitution and permitted no opposition parties, so banning parties that threaten the socialist order is accepted.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred: the critique of wage labour holds workers unfree while dependent on owners' power, even without direct coercion, though the doctrine does not use this vocabulary.

separated-powers.rationale: Lenin attacks the separation of powers as bourgeois parliamentarism and the Soviet system unites legislative and executive power in the soviets under Party leadership.

vanguard-party.rationale: This is Lenin's central claim: workers alone reach only trade-union consciousness and need a party of professional revolutionaries.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The state is defined as the rule of workers and peasants, and the constitution sets social rights and distribution by work, though the framing is class rule rather than care for the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The constitution makes housing a state-guaranteed social right and socialist ownership the base of the system, so selling public housing off to tenants runs against it, though personal property in a home was allowed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: the 1977 Constitution guarantees no right to strike and Lenin treats trade-union struggle as subordinate to the party, so limits on industrial action fit a state that claims to rule for workers.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxism-Leninism traces poverty to class exploitation and the relations of production, and rejects the idea that population is the cause.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The doctrine bases unity on class and socialism, and the constitution outlaws national hostility while upholding equality of nations.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: Lenin wants officials elected, recallable and paid workers wages, but leadership runs through a disciplined vanguard party, not chance selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Lenin holds the dictatorship of the proletariat rests on force and is not bound by bourgeois legality, and Marxist-Leninist states used emergency repression against class enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state plans the socialist economy and sets prices, and fixing food prices in scarcity fits that model.

party-controls-media.rationale: The party is the leading force of the state, and press freedom is granted only in line with the interests of the people and socialism, which in practice meant party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The CPSU is the constitutional leading and guiding force of the state, and Marxist-Leninist states kept their armies under party command through political organs.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which rejects dividing workers by nation and favors equal rights for foreign workers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution demands that all officials be paid ordinary workmen's wages, and the Paris Commune model it endorses ends official privilege.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism makes decisions binding on every member once adopted, which is the core of Lenin's vanguard party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine treats the bourgeois supranational unions as capitalist and imperialist blocs, while favouring a voluntary union of socialist states, so it rejects pooling sovereignty in a union like the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred: the ideal is rule by soviets and the party, not a head of state with personal command; in practice the party, not the presidency, held control of the army, and the legislature's formal supremacy was proclaimed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist state treats religion as ideology to be superseded and separates church from state, so it has no place for a state church governed by bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: The doctrine is atheist and the 1977 Constitution separates church from state and schools, so clergy ruling the state is the opposite of its program.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's position, repeated in the doctrine, is that in an imperialist war workers should turn the war into civil war and work for their own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet state subordinated art to socialist construction and restricted works it judged harmful to the socialist outlook, though the justification was political and class-based rather than purely moral character.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: the party's leading role was permanent and leaders served until death or removal, but the doctrine's formal soviet model has elected organs, and adherents differ on term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution demands that all officials be elected and subject to recall at any time.

missingStatements.text: Agricultural land should be farmed collectively rather than by individual farmers.
missingStatements.rationale: Collectivization of agriculture was a defining policy of Marxist-Leninist states, with collective-farm property written into the constitution.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism inevitably leads to imperialism and wars between the great powers.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin's theory of imperialism as the highest stage of capitalism is a core tenet of the doctrine.

notes: Practice in Marxist-Leninist states often diverged from constitutional texts (secession, freedom of conscience, soviet power). Chinese and Vietnamese Marxism-Leninism today accepts markets and would answer the market and growth questions differently. Social questions such as abortion and homosexuality varied over time.
